# Play live streams

Play live streams with live-edge tracking, DVR windows, and stream-type detection.

> **Note**
>
> Using a pre-built [skin](./skins.md)? It already includes the controls shown here. You may still need the media or player setup in this guide. The component examples are for building your own player UI from individual [components](./ui-components.md).

## Installation

The examples use `<hlsjs-video>`, so install hls.js with the framework façade:

```bash
pnpm add @videojs/html @videojs/hlsjs-video
```

## Recommended approach

Use the live feature bundle with a streaming media component, and give users a `<media-live-button>`: it shows whether playback is at the live edge and seeks back to it when activated.

```html
<live-video-player>
  <media-container>
    <hlsjs-video src="https://your-stream.example.com/live.m3u8" autoplay muted playsinline></hlsjs-video>
    <media-live-button></media-live-button>
  </media-container>
</live-video-player>
<script type="module">
  import '@videojs/html/live-video/player';
  import '@videojs/html/media/hlsjs-video';
  import '@videojs/html/live-video/ui';
</script>
```

The examples use [`<hlsjs-video>`](../reference/components/hlsjs-video.md). The smaller [`<hls-video>`](../reference/components/hls-video.md) also reports live state; use it when its supported feature set fits your stream.

The `liveVideoFeatures` bundle starts from [`videoFeatures`](./features.md), adds the live feature, and omits playback rate, quality selection, and audio-track selection. The live presets also ship skins without a time slider, duration display, or current-time display.

Both bundles are plain arrays, so extending one is a spread:

```ts
import { createPlayer, streamTypeFeature } from '@videojs/html';
import { liveVideoFeatures } from '@videojs/html/live-video';

const { PlayerElement } = createPlayer({ features: [...liveVideoFeatures, streamTypeFeature] });

customElements.define('custom-live-player', PlayerElement);
```

Use `<custom-live-player>` in place of `<live-video-player>` for this configuration.

## How it works

Two features describe liveness:

- The [stream type feature](../reference/api/feature-stream-type.md) reports `streamType`: `'live'`, `'on-demand'`, or `'unknown'`. Streaming media derives it from manifest metadata; plain media elements fall back to duration-based detection. `liveVideoFeatures` does not include it; add `streamTypeFeature` to the player’s features when you need `streamType`.
- The [live feature](../reference/api/feature-live.md) reports two values:
  - `liveEdgeStart` is where “live” begins on the timeline. When the playhead is at or past this time, the viewer is watching live; behind it, they’re watching earlier moments of the stream.
  - `targetLiveWindow` describes the kind of live window: `0` for a sliding window, `Infinity` for an event with playback history, and `NaN` for on-demand or unknown content. Read `seekable` to find the actual times viewers can rewind to.

The [time feature](../reference/api/feature-time.md) replaces an infinite media duration with the end of the seekable range. That end advances as new segments become available; the start can also advance as old segments expire.

`<media-live-button>` treats playback as live when the playhead is no more than five seconds behind `liveEdgeStart`. If `liveEdgeStart` is unknown, the button uses the last ten seconds of the seekable range instead. When playback is farther behind, activating the button seeks to the seekable end. The button is disabled (`data-disabled`) when the media is not live or has no finite seekable end. At the edge, it is inactive (`aria-disabled="true"`).

## Availability and constraints

- `liveEdgeStart` and `targetLiveWindow` require media that implements the live capability. Examples include [hls.js video](../reference/components/hlsjs-video.md), [SPF HLS video](../reference/components/hls-video.md), [native HLS video](../reference/components/native-hls-video.md), and [Shaka video](../reference/components/shaka-video.md). Native HLS video requires browser HLS support. A plain `<video>` can report a live `streamType` from its duration, but its live-window values stay `NaN`.
- Live playback drifts behind the edge when the network stalls or the tab is backgrounded. Always give users a path back to the edge.
- Both sliding live windows and growing event histories can support seeking. Check `seekable` for the available range. The built-in time slider starts at zero, so use it only while the seekable history starts at zero; a moving start requires a custom slider.
- `liveVideoFeatures` omits playback rate control. Add it explicitly if your DVR UI needs it.

## Common variations

### DVR: let users scrub back

For a live event whose seekable history starts at zero, add a [`<media-time-slider>`](../reference/components/time-slider.md) to your custom UI or [customized live skin](./customize-skins.md#style-skin-source). Its maximum follows the seekable end. For a sliding window whose start moves forward, build a slider from the current `seekable` start and end; the built-in slider would include expired times.

### Switch UI by stream type

Render live or on-demand controls from `streamType` when one player handles both kinds of content. Add `streamTypeFeature` to the player’s features; `liveVideoFeatures` does not include it:

`<media-live-button>` already reflects live state. To show a whole group of controls only for live streams, compose a custom player and subscribe to its store:

```html
<stream-type-player>
  <media-container>
    <hlsjs-video src="https://your-stream.example.com/live.m3u8" autoplay muted playsinline></hlsjs-video>
    <div id="live-controls" hidden>
      <media-live-button></media-live-button>
    </div>
  </media-container>
</stream-type-player>
<script type="module">
  import { createPlayer, selectStreamType, streamTypeFeature } from '@videojs/html';
  import { liveVideoFeatures } from '@videojs/html/live-video';
  import '@videojs/html/media/hlsjs-video';
  import '@videojs/html/ui/container';
  import '@videojs/html/ui/live-button';

  const { PlayerElement } = createPlayer({
    features: [...liveVideoFeatures, streamTypeFeature],
  });
  customElements.define('stream-type-player', PlayerElement);

  const player = document.querySelector('stream-type-player');
  const store = player.store;
  const controls = document.querySelector('#live-controls');
  const update = () => {
    controls.hidden = selectStreamType(store.state)?.streamType !== 'live';
  };

  const unsubscribe = store.subscribe(update);
  update();
  // Call unsubscribe() when this player is removed.
</script>
```

## Troubleshooting

### The live badge never activates

`<media-live-button>` reads `targetLiveWindow`, `currentTime`, and `seekable`. Confirm that `targetLiveWindow` is `0` or `Infinity` and that `seekable` has a finite end. Use a live-capable media component such as [`<hlsjs-video>`](../reference/components/hlsjs-video.md). The live button does not need `streamTypeFeature`; add it only when your own UI reads `streamType`.

### Playback keeps falling behind the edge

Network throughput can’t sustain the stream, or the tab was backgrounded. `<media-live-button>` returns users to the edge; for lower drift, review the stream’s latency configuration on the encoder side.

### The time slider behaves oddly on a live stream

Compare the slider’s range with `seekable`. The built-in slider always starts at zero. Once a sliding window moves past zero, the slider’s range includes expired history. Use a custom slider that follows both range bounds, or keep the live button without a timeline.
